text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Polish astronomer NICOLAS COPERNICUS, who developed the theory that the Earth and other planets revolved around the Sun, was born on this day in 1473.
Actress MERLE OBERON, whose many films included "THE SCARLET PIMPERNEL", "WUTHERING HEIGHTS" and "A SONG TO REMEMBER", was born in 1911. She claimed to have been born in Tasmania.

American actor LEE MARVIN, the tough-guy actor with the gravelly voice, was born on this day in 1924. He murmured the words to a song in the film "Paint Your Wagon". "Wandrin' Star" (1970) beame a hit. He died of heart failure in 1987.

American singer SMOKEY (WILLIAM) ROBINSON was born in 1940. He wrote countless hits for himself and others. He formed his first group the 'Matadors' while still at school. They eventually became the 'Miracles' and in 1958 they released "Got A Job" as their first single. Their first million seller on Motown records came in 1960 with "Shop Around". Other hits
included "You've Really Got A Hold On Me" (1962) and "The Tears Of A Clown" (1970). In 1972 SMOKEY left the group and released solo albums on a regular basis.
British guitarist with 'Black Sabbath' TONY IOMMI was born in 1949.
The Duke of York, Prince ANDREW ALBERT CHRISTIAN EDWARD (second son of QUEEN ELIZABETH II) who married SARAH FERGUSON in 1986 (now separated), was born in 1960.
Lead singer with the pop group "Frankie Goes To Hollywood", HOLLY JOHNSON, was born in 1960.
** EVENTS **
1405 : Tatar conqueror Timur-i-Lenk, also known as
Tamerlane, died while on his way to conquer China. He had already subdued lands stretching from northern India to the Mediterranean.
1800 : NAPOLEON BONAPARTE proclaimed himself First Consul
of the French dictatorship.
1897 : French tightrope artist CHARLES BLONDIN, who
walked across the Niagara Falls, died.
1906 : A new kind of 'instant' breakfast went on sale in

the United States. The BATTLE CREEK TOASTED CORNFLAKE COMPANY of Michigan (founded by WILL K. KELLOGG) had been developing the "flakes" for 30 years. Dr KELLOGG, a Seventh Day Adventist, had used the flakes as a vegetarian health food for patients with
mental illnesses.
1909 : Keen big game hunter, United States President
THEODORE ROOSEVELT, called for a world conference on conservation.
1921 : French engineer ETIENNE OECHMICHEN flew the first
successful helicopter test flight.
1942 : 243 people died in the first Japanese strike on
the Australian mainland during World War II. Japanese aircraft attacked Darwin, and surrounding military bases.
1945 : The U.S. Fifth Fleet launched the invasion of Iwo
Jima against the Japanese. The island was eventually taken on March 26 at the cost of 6,821 U.S. killed.
1948 : Sixteen RAAF personnel were killed when a Lincoln
bomber crashed at Amberley airbase in south-east Queensland.
1951 : JEAN LEE became the last woman hanged in
Australia. LEE, NORMAN ANDREWS and ROBERT CLAYTON were hanged in Melbourne for murder.
1961 : BARRY JONES, who went on to became a Federal
Cabinet Minister, won a record 13,000 pounds on BOB DYER's quiz show "Pick-a-Box".
1972 : The last RAAF aircraft left Vietnam for home. The
final Australian troops left in December 72 after ten years of fighting in the war.
1980 : Australian/British singer with 'AC/DC' BON SCOTT
died after a night of heavy drinking. He choked on his own vomit. He was 33.
1983 : Former journalist BRIAN BURKE led Labor to victory
in the West Australian state election, ending 9 years of conservative rule.
1991 : Russian President BORIS YELTSIN demanded the
resignation of Soviet President MIKHAIL GORBACHEV, as the USSR's two most influential men prepared for a drawn-out power struggle.
1993 : More than 1200 people drowned when a crowded ferry
sank off the coast of Haiti.
1994 : Fire bombs damaged six London stores; the IRA
claimed responsiblility.
